script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Wednesday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed one point three eight percent down on the session. A rough day, driven by a single headline that blindsided the semiconductor space.

Elon Musk confirmed that SpaceX will use Nvidia chips exclusively for its artificial intelligence workloads. That statement landed directly on Advanced Micro Devices, sending it down seven point zero four percent — the worst single-session loss in this portfolio Wednesday.

The broader market told a more nuanced story. The Dow Jones Industrial Average posted a record high Wednesday, lifted by Nvidia and aided by diplomatic progress on the Strait of Hormuz. The Nasdaq, however, underperformed, weighed down by mega-cap communication services names and select technology names caught in the Musk-Nvidia narrative. No Federal Reserve data or major economic prints were on the calendar to shift rate expectations during the session.

Advanced Micro Devices dominated the news flow Wednesday, and the damage warrants a full accounting. The company was already facing what analysts describe as valuation fatigue heading into earnings season — Seeking Alpha rated the stock a Hold, noting that second-quarter growth projections cannot justify current multiples. Then came the Musk announcement. SpaceX's exclusive commitment to Nvidia chips removes a high-profile potential customer from the Advanced Micro Devices pipeline and sends a signal to the broader market about competitive positioning in the AI accelerator race. Fortune and Yahoo Finance both flagged the stock as a primary drag on the Nasdaq. As the largest position in this portfolio at eight point three nine percent, a seven point zero four percent single-session drop carries real weight. The question now is whether institutional holders treat this as a buying opportunity or a structural warning about market share in AI compute.

Advanced Micro Devices was down seven point zero four percent on the session — the portfolio's heaviest holding, and Wednesday's clear underperformer. The Musk-SpaceX headline is the catalyst to track into next week, particularly any response from management or updates to competitive positioning against Nvidia in AI workloads.

Micron Technology was up just zero point zero six percent on the session — essentially unchanged. It was a volatile path to flat, however. Shares rose earlier in the day after positive commentary from Musk about surging memory prices, then retreated sharply once the SpaceX-Nvidia exclusive story emerged. Separately, Yahoo Finance noted that a current memory shortage may be creating the conditions for a future industry oversupply problem — a dynamic worth watching over the next several quarters for this position.

Nvidia was up three point four three percent on the session — the standout gainer across the primary holdings Wednesday. The SpaceX exclusive endorsement was the direct driver. With a seven point six one percent portfolio weight, that move provided meaningful positive offset to the day's losses.

Broadcom was up zero point zero three percent — essentially flat. Seeking Alpha upgraded the stock to Buy Wednesday, citing artificial intelligence compute leadership and supply chain positioning. A marginal session, but analyst sentiment is constructive.

Intel was up zero point two zero percent on the session. No major company-specific news Wednesday. The stock continues to trade as a turnaround story, and any read-through from the broader AI chip narrative will remain a key factor.

Turning to the equipment names — Applied Materials was down two point two six percent on the session. No specific news drove the move. The stock likely traded in sympathy with broader semiconductor weakness tied to the Advanced Micro Devices sell-off.

KLA Corporation was down one point three six percent Wednesday. Again, no discrete catalyst. Equipment names broadly underperformed as sentiment soured on semiconductor end-demand visibility.

Marvell Technology was down three point four six percent on the session. No direct news, but the stock has AI-infrastructure exposure, and the Musk-Nvidia exclusive commentary likely pressured names seen as competing or adjacent to Nvidia's ecosystem.

Over at Lam Research, shares were down three point two five percent on the session. No specific headline, but the equipment sector moved lower in concert with the broader semiconductor weakness across the portfolio Wednesday.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was down zero point seven six percent — a relatively contained move given the session's volatility. No direct news, but as the foundry underpinning nearly every major chip name in this portfolio, macro and geopolitical signals, including Strait of Hormuz developments, remain the primary variables to monitor.

Three items to track in the next forty-eight hours. First, any formal response or guidance update from Advanced Micro Devices management regarding the SpaceX-Nvidia exclusive announcement — investor relations communication or conference appearances could move the stock materially. Second, Micron Technology's trajectory in the memory pricing cycle — the Yahoo Finance report flagging a potential future oversupply condition deserves close attention, particularly if additional commentary emerges from industry participants. Third, watch for any follow-on analyst revisions across the equipment names — Applied Materials, Lam Research, and KLA Corporation all moved lower without discrete catalysts, and institutional commentary in the next session could clarify whether those moves reflect repositioning or something more structural.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch for any response from Advanced Micro Devices and whether Nvidia can hold Wednesday's gains as the market processes the full implications of the SpaceX announcement.
